## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (66%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Invasive · Careful review
InSitu (34%) stays in the 90% conformal set, though a second model agrees on Invasive [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 66%, InSitu 34% | Close two-class split |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / 1.0 | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees on Invasive |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Invasive | Mixed; two InSitu |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 5, 9) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; concept model links it to invasion [F3] · Validated
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (regions 1, 6, 8) · ↑ invasive · Scored above typical; failed spot check, 0/20 acceptable [F4] · Unreliable
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 1, 4) · ↑ invasive · Scored high; spot check only 3/20 acceptable · Unreliable
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 4, 8, 9) · context · Above typical; descriptive only; spot check 8/20 [F2] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so unvalidated; this case leans on unreliable mitoses and necrosis.

## Could be wrong if
- True class is InSitu: it holds 34%, and two of five similar cases are InSitu.
- Concept support for Invasive is mostly unreliable cues (mitoses, necrosis); only stroma is validated.

## Check on the slide
1. **0, 5, 9**: Confirm tumor cells infiltrate stroma rather than staying within ducts.
2. **1, 6, 8**: Count mitoses yourself; the model's mitosis score failed its spot check.
3. **0, 1, 8**: Verify tumor at margin; simulated frozen section calls all four margins involved [F7].
